description:
_parse_work_flag (_project/scripts/todo_db.py ~4603) parses WID:SUMMARY[:needs=w1,w2] as:

    parts = spec.split(':', 2)
    if len(parts) == 3 and parts[2].startswith('needs='):
        needs = ...
    work.append({'id': parts[0], 'summary': parts[1], 'needs': needs})

When SUMMARY itself contains a colon, split(':', 2) puts the tail in parts[2]. That tail does not start with 'needs=', so the needs branch is skipped, parts[2] is DISCARDED, and the summary is silently truncated at the first colon. Any needs= clause that followed is lost with it. No error, no warning, exit 0.

Observed live while filing worktree-release-force-does-not-force-past-dirty-tree-20260806:

  --add-work 'w2:Regression coverage: a dirty pool slot releases and resets under FORCE=1:needs=w1'
  stored -> summary 'Regression coverage', needs []

Two units of information were destroyed by one flag: most of the summary, and the w1 dependency that would have ordered the unit. The item looked fine in the create output; the loss is only visible on a later show.

INCONSISTENT WITH ITS SIBLINGS
- _parse_work_edits (~2206), backing --edit-work, uses split(':', 1) and therefore PRESERVES colons in the summary. So the same text survives --edit-work but is truncated by --work/--add-work. That is why repairing the unit above worked.
- _parse_verify_flag (~4616) uses '::' as its field separator, which is the right shape for free text and should be the model to copy.

FIX OPTIONS (a is the minimum, b is the ergonomic one)
a. Fail loudly. If len(parts) == 3 and parts[2] does not start with 'needs=', raise TodoError instead of discarding. Backward compatible, converts silent data loss into a visible error.
b. Parse the needs clause off the END rather than by position. Detect a trailing ':needs=...' suffix and treat everything before it as the summary. Makes colons in summaries just work, matching --edit-work.
c. Consider accepting '::' as the needs separator for symmetry with --verify, keeping ':needs=' as a deprecated alias.

Also note there is no --drop-work, so a unit added with a mangled summary can only be repaired via --edit-work (summary only). A lost needs= clause cannot be restored at all without recreating the item.

Scope note: this is a tracker CLI defect and touches no benchmark code.

preserves.behavior: Well-formed WID-SUMMARY and WID-SUMMARY-needs specs keep their current parse and stored result
